claims.text: An integrated machine-learning and ab initio phonon-calculation workflow can accurately identify new HEA compositions with ultralow phonon thermal conductivity.
The integrated workflow will outperform conventional thermal-conductivity prediction approaches.
First-principles calculations can provide data on structural and chemical behavior in HEAs.
Machine learning can screen large HEA compositional spaces for low thermal conductivity.
The range 200–800 K represents typical cryogenic, ambient, and elevated-temperature insulation conditions.
High configurational disorder throughout a multi-element HEA lattice causes significant phonon scattering.
Disorder-induced phonon scattering reduces intrinsic phonon transport.
Learning composition–structure–property relations from ab initio data improves predictive accuracy.
The predictive workflow can identify chemical disorder that impedes phonon propagation.
The proposed workflow will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy by approximately 20% or more relative to conventional approaches.
The workflow will enable discovery of HEA compositions with significantly lower thermal conductivity for insulation.
Rule-of-mixtures or simplified phenomenological models are the relevant existing baseline for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in complex alloys.
The approach is applicable to HEAs in which phonons dominate thermal transport over moderately wide composition ranges.
The approach is less applicable when electronic or magnon heat transport dominates.
The approach is less applicable at extremely high temperatures because additional effects become significant.
Extrapolation to compositions or temperatures absent from the training data may reduce predictive performance.
Laser-flash analysis across the target temperature range can provide the measurements needed to benchmark predicted HEA thermal conductivities.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% accuracy improvement over conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
